notes: The tutorial has two separate circuits (sender and receiver), both included in one graph: mkr1/bb1/btn1 are the sender, mkr2/bb2/led1/r1 the receiver. Both are kept because the manual builds both.

The MKR WAN 1300 and the antenna are not in the catalogue, so they were added as new part types. To fix the lug-to-lug validation error, the antenna FEED port is now kind 'wire-end' and the board ANT port is kind 'header-socket'. This is a compatible pair. The board USB port stays a 'lug'.
Breadboard coordinates are read from the images. The picture's upper half (rows j-f) is bank 'b' and the lower half (rows e-a) is bank 't'.
Only two pushbutton legs are visible, at columns 5 and 7. They are modelled as 1.l and 2.l, so one leg is on each switch side. The side-to-leg mapping is a guess.
In the sender, GND (black) goes to the button's col-5 strip and pin 2 (yellow) to the col-7 strip. Pin 2 uses INPUT_PULLUP, so pressing the button pulls pin 2 to GND.
In the receiver, the LED cathode is in column 6 with the GND wire (black). The LED anode is in column 8 and the resistor runs from column 8 to column 11. The pin 2 wire (green) is in column 11.
The resistor value is not stated, so 220 ohm is assumed. The image shows red bands.

The manual lists a micro USB cable for each board, so they are included. They are joined only to the boards; the laptops are not modelled. The usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports, so the cable side port is null.
Nothing is shown connected to the breadboard power rails.
